newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank says not trying to lower peso.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank says not trying to lower peso.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Monday it was not trying to push down the peso, despite last Friday's hike in its dollar rate.

"Of course not. If that was the case why was it (the dollar rate) moved down again on Monday," Treasurer Sergio Edeza told reporters, when asked if the Central Bank was signalling it wanted the peso to depreciate.
The peso fell to a 32-month low at the end of last week after the Bank increased its dollar bid/offer quote to 26.290/26.390 pesos, up from 26.275/26.375.
However, on Monday it lowered its rate.
Edeza said Friday's move was simply in response to pre-weekend arbitrage.

"We don't want banks arbitraging at the expense of the Central Bank. We make sure we are there to spoil the fun. It's just okay for them to do arbitrage play among themselves but not with the Central Bank," he said.
